priorFindingResolutions.assessment: Every trusted Ed public key is converted to exactly 32 bytes, parsed with ed25519-dalek VerifyingKey::from_bytes and rejected when is_weak. Ticket verification decodes the signature and calls verify_strict on the original JWS signing input before JWT claim decoding. The trusted JWT key and strict key are built from the same bytes. This closes the configured identity-key unsigned-grant reproduction.
priorFindingResolutions.actualVerification: Committed malformed-length and weak-key regressions passed. The independent artifact probe also rejected zero and identity public-key configurations and an identity-R/zero-S unsigned token under a strong trusted key, with otherwise valid scope/policy. Fresh real Node/PG grants still verified; the existing Rust harness rejected forgery and all 18 freshly signed negatives.

priorFindingResolutions.assessment: Each TrustDomain creates a private Arc instance identity, retained by its admitted sessions. with_authorized rejects a non-identical instance before checking or invoking effects. Session fields are private; external code cannot mint or alter the admitted claims/domain. A surviving session retains the allocation, preventing identity reuse after its original domain is dropped. Equal nonce/expiry therefore cannot transfer a session across domains.
priorFindingResolutions.actualVerification: The committed private-state unit regression passed. An independent public-API probe generated two real Ed25519-signed grants with disjoint trusted key sets, different subjects/sessions, equal nonce/expiry and identical runtime scope. The receiving domain installed valid policy for both identities, rejected the foreign token signature, admitted its own ticket, and rejected the foreign session with Replay and zero foreign effects. Local sessions executed with their correct identity. A second case admitted the same signed ticket in two instances and rejected cross-instance handles while allowing each local handle.

additionalCorrectionAssessment: with_authorized now requires a unit-returning callback and returns Result<(), TrustError>. The committed async-returning callback compile-fail doctest passed. This closes the specific generic Future return escape from slice1; it does not prevent a unit callback from copying identity or scheduling work.

The tightened native world-label validator agrees with the issuer's lowercase/digit-leading, maximum-64-character suffix contract. No new service, production key, transport or persistence activation is included in this correction.
